Level 3 additionally requires assessed collaboration to recur across the program AND at least one assessment to require coordinating work across people AND tools/AI systems (documented role/tool allocation). Collaborative assessment does recur across Years 1-2, but no captured unit documents an assessment of the division of work between people and AI/tool systems, and the Year 3 Engineering Capstone (ENGR90037/38) - the most plausible site for such a task - has no assessment page in the extract. Ambiguity resolves to the lower level per the scoring-direction rule.

C2.rationale: Level 2 met via criterion-referenced peer review: ENGR90051's assessed 'Peer feedback + evaluation' is structured critique of peers' contribution, satisfying the anchor's peer-review/structured-critique clause. Level 3 requires assessment that documents and justifies reliance decisions on a tool, source or collaborator, or evidences strategy adjustment over time (process-focused assessment). The fortnightly 'Project log' plus the final individual 'Reflection' could be read that way, but the extract only describes them as general reflection tied to project logs, not explicitly as documenting reliance decisions or strategy adjustment. This matches the anchor's tool-operation/training clause - 'the operational level TEQSA identifies as non-durable' - which caps the score at 1 regardless of core/elective status. C4.rationale: Level 2 met: ENGR90051 (core) requires assessed engagement with a real-world, complex, cross-context problem - matching the anchor's 'cross-context projects' example of application to novel or unfamiliar problems - via graded project logs, review, demonstration and final submission, not merely claimed in outcomes. The course overview states the degree 'culminates in a capstone design experience' (ENGR90037/38), which could satisfy this, but no assessment page for the capstone subjects was present in the extract, so the self-scoping/progression structure cannot be confirmed. C5.rationale: Level 1 (R2 default): the program-level ILO documents a research capability - 'undertake a piece of original research... involving the collection of data, its objective analysis and interpretation' - but this appears only among program-level intended learning outcomes, with no core-unit assessment evidence for it in the extract. Per R2, a capability documented in outcomes but never shown to be assessed scores 1 uniformly. W1.rationale: Level 1 met: professional communication and 'purposeful' stakeholder interaction appear in ILOs, and core assessment adds spoken/interactive components (interactive discussion, team demonstration) beyond the teaching-team default of exams/reports. Level 2 requires a recognised professional genre or an audience beyond the teaching team (client brief, pitch, public-facing artefact) judged against practice-derived criteria. The extract documents stakeholder interaction as an ILO and an assessed 'Interactive discussion' and 'Demonstration,' but never states the audience is external to the teaching team or names a specific professional genre judged against professional-practice criteria. Ambiguity resolves to the lower level.
evidenceLines: Demonstrate effective engineering communication skills, including the ability to articulate design concepts and technical information to achieve specific outcomes, and to purposefully interact with a range of stakeholders.

W2.rationale: Level 2 clearly met: at least one core assessment (ENGR90051) reproduces a professional engineering-design task end to end - problem definition through prototyping and testing on a real-world problem - and MCEN30021 and MCEN90061 similarly run assessed hands-on design/build projects with real-world framing, i.e. the artefact and process resemble what a practitioner produces. Level 3 requires such tasks to form the program's assessment spine (a capstone plus scaffolding, or at least one per stage) AND at least one to carry a genuine constraint of practice. Years 1-2 show a strong recurring pattern and ENGR90051's stakeholder/sustainability/safety/ethics-constrained brief looks like a genuine practice constraint, but the Year 3 capstone (ENGR90037/38) assessment page is absent from the extract, so continuation of the spine into the final stage is unconfirmed. Ambiguity resolves to the lower level.

W3.rationale: Level 1 met: the Engineering Practice Hurdle documents work-situated learning only as one of several optional routes - STEP (a skills/employability program, not a supervised placement), the ENGR90033 Internship subject (confirmed elsewhere as a Group B elective, 25 credit points), or an unassessed self-arranged internship 'without receiving University credit.' None of these is a required, supervised, assessed core placement, matching the anchor's 'exists only as an elective, an optional internship, or an unassessed extracurricular... activity.' No core unit places students in a supervised, assessed real workplace setting, so Level 0 is also excluded by the presence of these routes.
